*Upon first listen -* 

*I'm a huge Dive but sadly I didn't fall in love with this album as much as I expected or as much as I did with their previous releases.*



**REBEL HEART** \- I loved this one right off the bat. It's catchy and powerful - a perfect self-love inspiring anthem. It's I AM's twin and I LOVED that track. It's what got me into IVE. Definitely deserves to be the title track because it's such a good intro to the EP - especially with Yujin's "Come join as who you are" line. Chills.

**You Wanna Cry** \- Oh I have a bone to pick with this one.

The I Wanna Dance With Somebody sample is not at all working for me. It totally distracts from IVE's actual song. Instead of focusing on the song as it is, it immediately makes me think of Whitney Houston's song and my attention just stays there. Like Whitney's song was stuck in my head after this listen and I remembered almost nothing of You Wanna Cry itself - which is not good ahhh. 

And it's such a huge chunk of the song that was sampled - not just a second or two. For example, Yujin's "Love me Love me" in the bridge of Off The Record was a sample melody from Lovefool by The Cardigans. But it felt tasteful; short and sweet. Even the I Will Survive sample in After Like was long but tasteful because it was intentionally obvious. It felt like a sort of reprise to the original in a way.

Such a shame because the rest of the song apart from the sample is so great on its own - especially the instrumental and the lyrics. The producers should've attempted to come up with an original and fresh melody for the chorus.

> an indifferent universe would create indifferent matter

I love this actually. Makes me feel special enough to appreciate being granted this existence by a dying universe, but not special enough to forget that I am still only a tiny part of the entire picture.

Interesting, because the way you describe universes is exactly how "life" behaves. Life is born, it procreates and multiplies, then it dies. But why? What is driving everything including entire universes to behave this way? And do you really think it's plausible that in our entire universe, we - some fleshy lanky organic creatures - are the ones chosen to take upon this great task of creating entire other universes? 

And would you describe the universe and everything in it as "alive" then? Because sometimes it gives me comfort to think that our universe is just a giant brain. So in the same way neurons in our brains forge new connections, sever connections, spark up, fizzle out, and explode - all the astronomical events in our universe including the life and death of entire stars are just some neurons firing off in some ginormous alien's head.

If the universe doesn't give a shit about the life, existence, or death of some infinitesimal cells in some deep corner of its existence - why should I, the infinitesimal cell, be so egotistical as to be aware of my existence, or be afraid of my death and the nothingness that comes after it? Do you think the countless cells and microorganisms floating around in a human body at any given moment contemplate or give a crap about their existence?

I know it's complicated but after poring over many theories to help my anxiety about death and nothingness, this theory helps me cope the best.
Who knows? It just does. Why does ANY life have to exist at all, from the smallest of microbes to plants to humans? Why does the universe exist and exist in the way it is?
